bullets.title: Semis/Nasdaq sold off hard on yield spike and Iran fears
bullets.body: The semiconductor index dropped 5% (SOXX failed at the 50-day MA), Nasdaq fell 1.35% to 26,285, and S&P fell 0.66% to 7,694. 10-year Treasury yield hit highest since Jan 2025 (~4.70%), 30-year hit 5.31–5.34% (highest since 2007); commentary describes the move as bond-market repricing of reflation rather than panic (BBB spreads unchanged). One fintwit account warns 'Tech ignored rates for months — the bill may be coming due.'

bullets.title: NYSE breadth divergence at record levels — bearish divergence last seen Dec 2021
bullets.body: More than 3x as many NYSE securities hitting 52-week lows as highs while SPY sits ~2% from all-time highs. One account notes 'we have never seen such a decoupling between price and breadth' — last comparable divergence preceded the 2022 drawdown. Hindenburg Omen also triggered 15 times in past 3 months, historically associated with major corrections.

bullets.title: Optical supply chain remains severely under-supplied; LITE, MTSI, AAOI all confirm
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts citing earnings from LITE, MTSI, and AAOI showing 'extreme demand imbalances in lasers, TIA and DSP.' AAOI management stated the company is 'sold out at least through second half of next year and beyond,' with capacity booked through Q2 2027. Silicon photonics commercial production described as 'accelerating across leading foundries and IDMs' with COHR wireline delivering record orders, more than doubling YoY.

bullets.title: NBIS: Pennsylvania data center executive order moderately negative but not thesis-breaking
bullets.body: Investment committee analysis characterizes Pennsylvania Gov. Shapiro's Aug. 18 data center executive order as 'materially more consequential than a conventional environmental-policy statement' but 'materially less absolute than social-media language implies.' Not a project cancellation; power procurement framework under PJM ('bring, build or buy') adds complexity. CEG flagged as clearest relative beneficiary among PA power suppliers given Crane/Three Mile Island project with MSFT.

bullets.title: NVDA: $105B OpenAI Ohio guarantee; Groq raises at half valuation with NVDA in round
bullets.body: Nvidia backed OpenAI's Ohio campus with a $105B guarantee. Separately, Groq raised $350M at roughly half last year's valuation with Nvidia participating — one analyst notes concern about capital raises given Nvidia's recent large-scale M&A activity. LG Electronics accelerating robotics pact with Nvidia.

bullets.title: MRVL: $3.25B acquisition under scrutiny — 2026 paper is process evidence only, no performance data
bullets.body: Deep-dive thread on what Marvell acquired for $3.25B (closed Feb 2): ECTC papers by same authors one year apart, with domain shifted from 'Assembly Process' to 'Demonstration.' The 2026 paper provides only process evidence with no new optical characterization data; reliability testing listed as future work. Assembly planned 2025, potential product delivery ~2027.

bullets.title: PCB price hikes 5–30% in 1H26; fresh hikes signaled for 2H26 as CCL/prepreg tightens
bullets.body: Taiwan PCB makers raised quoted prices 5–30% in 1H 2026 as copper-clad laminates and prepreg supply tightened. Industry sources now whispering another round of hikes in 2H 2026. Resin prices (used to make prepreg) rising quickly. Intel Malaysia reportedly absorbing TSMC CoWoS overflow as packaging orders surge.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler IG debt approaching big-bank scale; data center credit crowding out Treasuries
bullets.body: Hyperscaler investment-grade debt on pace to grow from $288B to $659B in two years, approaching levels of major US/non-US banks. IG supply forecast at $1.9T in 2026, exceeding the 2020 record of $1.66T. One account describes data center credit growth as 'crowding out US Treasury bond sales.' 10-year MACD broke upward, signaling possible new bond bear phase.

bullets.title: Anthropic overtakes OpenAI in quarterly revenue; AI ARR acceleration accelerating
bullets.body: Anthropic Q2 revenue hit $11.6B (more than doubled), surpassing OpenAI's $6.7B (+18% QoQ) for the first time. Anthropic's 14-fold annual revenue surge described as anchoring AI chip demand ahead of a potential record IPO. OpenAI and Anthropic ARR growth also confirmed to have accelerated YoY in July, contradicting 2nd-derivative slowdown narrative.

bullets.title: AAOI: Government funding for domestic optics capacity to displace Chinese suppliers already underway
bullets.body: AAOI management noted at Rosenblatt conference that the US may need government funding to replace Chinese optics — and indicated that funding is already occurring. Author cross-references ALMU as a related beneficiary. AAOI described as 'sold out' with capacity booked through Q2 2027.

bullets.title: META: $1.4T penalty risk in federal trial; talent disadvantage vs. space/search/AI also flagged
bullets.body: Four state AGs (CA, CO, KY, NJ) filed consumer protection suit against META with trial in Oakland; calculated penalty exposure up to $1.4T. Separately, commentary argues great engineers prefer space/search/AI companies over ad-tech, and Zuckerberg avoids the topic. Hedgeye analysis also cited: 'Meta's biggest threat isn't AI.'

bullets.title: GLW: $3.1M institutional call sweep signals bullish bet on AI-fiber capacity build
bullets.body: A $3.1M long-dated $200 call sweep with 34x volume-to-open-interest ratio was flagged in Corning, linked to the company's AI fiber capacity expansion thesis.

bullets.title: GOOGL: All 'Attention Is All You Need' co-authors have now left Google
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis podcast highlights that every co-author of the seminal transformer paper has departed Google — Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat to Discovery Loop, Noam Shazeer to OpenAI, John Jumper to Anthropic, Demis Hassabis stepping back from DeepMind. Google's talent exodus and cultural issues identified as key headwinds; one account draws the Google/See's Candies/Berkshire analogy for search vs. AI bet.

bullets.title: Trump pauses 50% Canada tariffs 3 days pending deal; deal reported reached pending finalization
bullets.body: Trump paused 50% Canadian tariffs through Aug. 21; Trump later stated a deal was reached awaiting document finalization. USTR Greer says deal includes market access and economic security commitments. USD/CAD fell 0.2% to C$1.3877 on the news. Auto sector remains the main sticking point.

bullets.title: US-Iran tensions: Strait of Hormuz at 6 vessel crossings/day; oil at $85 WTI / $91 Brent
bullets.body: Strait of Hormuz saw just 6 vessel crossings Tuesday (preliminary). Iran fired two ballistic missiles at UAE (both intercepted). Trump ordered all Iran talks halted. WTI settled at $84.94 (+0.52%); Brent at $91.02. U.S. diesel reserves at 23-year lows with crack spreads above $102/bbl. Iran Foreign Ministry says Strait won't reopen until US lifts blockade.

bullets.title: 30-year US Treasury hits 5.31–5.34%, highest since 2007; $25B auction clears at 5.216%
bullets.body: The US sold $25B of 30-year bonds at 5.216%, the highest yield in 25 years. The 30-year briefly hit 5.34% intraday. Dalio cited markets 'rising close to but not at levels seen in 2000 and 1929.' US national debt at $39.93T with $600B added since July 1. France's 30-year yield also hit highest since 2008 GFC.

bullets.title: INTC: Intel gaining advanced packaging share on TSMC as AI demand overwhelms supply
bullets.body: One account flags that 'Intel Malaysia took over advanced packaging for TSMC due to a surge in CoWoS orders from a major mutual client.' Intel reportedly gaining ground on TSMC's packaging dominance as AI demand overwhelms the industry leader. ASE, Unimicron, Gudeng Precision flagged as additional beneficiaries.

bullets.title: CRDO up 150% since March selling-exhaustion signal; all-time highs flagged as next target
bullets.body: One account notes CRDO identified as a selling-exhaustion buy in early March 2026 and is now up 150%, with all-time highs described as 'in sight.'

bullets.title: AAPL: Tepper reportedly bet against Apple in Q2 2026; EU App Store reforms underway
bullets.body: Hedge fund Q2 filings show Tepper took an unexpected bearish position against Apple and Berkshire. Separately, Apple is reforming EU App Store policies by cutting fee barriers and easing access for alternative stores under regulatory pressure.

bullets.title: TSLA: Semi page update highlights lower TCO vs. diesel; robotaxi safety monitor debate active
bullets.body: Tesla updated its Semi page emphasizing lower energy costs and fewer maintenance parts vs. diesel. On robotaxi, a critic argues Tesla vehicles still rely on safety monitors in the vast majority of deployments unlike Waymo, framing this as an autonomous capability gap.
